Hi Marta — looping in the technical detail as requested. High-level options and trade-offs: 

1) Hosted API (regional endpoints):
   - We currently offer EU regions (Frankfurt, Dublin) as isolated endpoints; data is stored and processed in-region.
   - APAC latency: if you direct APAC traffic to an EU-hosted endpoint, network RTT will add latency; not recommended for sub-200ms SLAs.

2) Dedicated (reserved capacity):
   - Can provision dedicated pools in a specific region (e.g., EU only) to guarantee residency.
   - Option: deploy a Dedicated pool in EU + edge-forwarding from APAC that only transmits anonymized or tokenized payloads. This reduces per-request data leaving APAC but requires transformations.

3) Private (VPC / on-prem):
   - Full control: deploy inside your VPC in an EU region or on-premises in your data center in APAC. Meets strict residency and in-country processing requirements.

Cross-region patterns to consider:
- Cross-region routing with regional model variants (e.g., run a smaller model in APAC for low-latency tasks and fall back to EU for high-quality/refined inference).
- Read-only KV/prefix caches at edge to reduce repeated tokenization costs without persisting customer PII outside EU.

Security & compliance: we can provide SOC2, encryption-at-rest/in-transit details, and KMS integration notes. Attached sample_msp_config.yaml shows a minimal VPC peering and routing config for Dedicated/Private setup.

Docs: https://redwood.ai/docs/deployments/regions

High-level cost delta (very rough) — subject to exact sizing:
- Hosted API (EU region): lowest up-front, usage-based; good for variable load but subject to multi-tenant capacity limits.
- Dedicated: higher monthly commitment, predictable throughput and easier SLA negotiation; better for heavy sustained inference.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): highest upfront engineering + possible infra CapEx; necessary when procurement requires on-prem or strict data control.
